subject: Support least-privilege design questions & milestones (post-demo)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finova.com>, Naveen Rao <naveen.rao@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Support least-privilege design questions & milestones (post-demo)

Hi Emily + Naveen — thanks again for taking the demo today. Great to see your team thinking through operational guardrails up front. As promised, quick recap and a concise set of clarifying questions so we can size and propose the design for support access and retention.

Summary (high level)
- Goal: Provide Finova support team with time-limited troubleshooting access while enforcing least-privilege roles, auditable break-glass for emergencies, and retention controls for PII and logs.
- Next deliverable from Redwood: a one-page support access design + retention matrix and a proposed canary rollout timeline.

Clarifying questions (we need your answers to finalize scope):
1) Primary PII classes: can you confirm the canonical list (SSN, bank account, card PAN, full name + DOB, customer identifiers)? Any other categories we must treat as PII for Finova?
2) Retention windows: for chat transcripts / generated content and access logs, do you have mandated windows (e.g., 30/90/365 days) or should we propose defaults?
3) Support roles: who on your side needs JIT support sessions (readonly vs. temporary write), and will you want Redwood to provide RBAC roles mapped to your IdP groups?
4) Break-glass escalation: acceptable approval path during incidents (Pager duty + exec token, Slack approval, or DocuSign-based sign-off)?
5) Residency constraints: any production data that must remain in us-east-1 only?

Immediate asks from us (these will shape the proposal):
- Please drop the canonical PII list and current retention policy (if any) into the Drive link below by EOD Tue 5/18.
- Confirm two technical contacts for implementation (SRE + Security).

Proposed internal timeline
- 5/18: Finova returns PII list + retention windows (you)
- 5/21: Redwood shares support access design (draft PDF) + retention matrix (spreadsheet)
- 5/26: Sizing & commercial proposal (includes canary plan and pricing for audit-retention)

Attachments: lightweight draft we used as demo artifact (support-privs-draft.pdf).

If anything above is off, tell me and I’ll adjust. Otherwise we’ll lock the 5/21 delivery and iterate.

Thanks —
Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finova.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naveen Rao <naveen.rao@finova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support least-privilege design questions & milestones (post-demo)

Hi Logan — appreciated the demo. Quick answers inline:

1) PII classes: confirm SSN (masked), bank account number (last 4), full name, DOB, address, internal customer_id, device identifiers. Card PAN is tokenized in our flows, but treat as sensitive if available.
2) Retention windows: logs (audit + access) must be retained 365 days; chat transcripts with customer content 180 days; generated model outputs 90 days unless tied to a ticket, where we keep 365 days. If Redwood has recommendations for shorter/longer windows based on cost, include them.
3) Support roles: we have tier-1 (support@finova.com) needing readonly + ephemeral debugger access; tier-2 (SRE) needing temporary elevated ops commands (max 1 hour sessions). We’d like RBAC mapped to Okta groups.
4) Break-glass: initial plan is Slack approval from Security lead + post-facto ticket in Jira. For high-risk events we require exec-level post-approval within 4 hours.
5) Residency: production PII must remain in us-east-1; logs may replicate to us-west for DR but must be encrypted and KMS-controlled.

Contacts: Myself (security lead) and Naveen (SRE). We’ll upload the current retention table to your Drive by EOD Tue 5/18.

Thanks —
Emily Zhao
Head of Security, Finova
emily.zhao@finova.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finova.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:56:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support least-privilege design questions & milestones (post-demo)

Emily — perfect, thanks for the specifics. Based on your constraints I sketched a support access flow and a retention matrix. Key calls we plan to include in the draft:

- RBAC model: three Redwood-managed roles we map to Okta groups: Support_Readonly, Support_Temp_Elevate, Support_Audit_Admin. All elevated sessions are JIT and time-boxed.
- JIT elevation: uses Okta OAuth + short-lived Redwood session. Elevation requires a Slack ack from Security lead OR Jira approval for non-emergency; emergency break-glass path uses a three-way (Pager -> Slack -> temporary token) and is logged immutably.
- Auditing: every support session emits: session start/end, operator identity, allowed actions list, model inputs (truncated to remove raw credentials), and a hashed pointer to the full transcript stored in our encrypted retention store.
- Retention controls: implement per-data-class TTLs, immutable append-only audit log retained 365 days, model outputs configurable per-workflow (90/180/365 per your guidance).

Open questions from implementation POV:
- Is Finova comfortable with Redwood holding encrypted audit logs under a Finova-managed KMS key (we support Bring-Your-Own-Key)?
- For session recordings/transcripts: do you prefer redaction (remove PII) before storage or encrypted storage with access gating? Redaction saves cost but is lossy; encrypted storage preserves fidelity for future investigations.

I attached the draft artifacts: finova-retention-matrix.xlsx and a breakglass-flow.drawio. I can turn these into a one-page design on 5/21.

Action items we’ll take on next: Ben to produce the one-page design, Marissa to align on SSO mapping and pricing impact.

-ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finova.com>, Naveen Rao <naveen.rao@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support least-privilege design questions & milestones (post-demo)

Thanks Emily — this is exactly what we need. Quick confirmation and next steps: 

- BYOK KMS: Redwood supports Finova-provided KMS keys; we will include configuration options in the draft.
- Transcripts: we’ll propose two options in the doc (redact-on-ingest vs encrypted-access-gated) and show cost delta.
- Timeline confirmed: we’ll deliver the one-page support access design + retention matrix by 5/21.

Please expect the design in Drive at the link below. If you want to schedule 30 minutes after delivery to walk it, I can set that up for 5/21 afternoon.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C
HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FD-4832

Next actions (owner / due):
- Finova: upload canonical PII & retention policy (Emily) / 5/18 — noted received.

Appreciate the clarity — we’ll aim for a design that minimizes risk while preserving debuggability.

Cheers,
Logan
